summary: The Battery Recycling for America's Competitive Economy Act (BRACE Act) changes how lithium-ion batteries are regulated under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act. It aims to make it easier to recycle lithium-ion batteries and recover critical minerals by allowing certain storage and recycling facilities to follow universal waste rules instead of stricter hazardous waste regulations.

affected_groups.effect: Allowed to follow large quantity handler of universal waste requirements and do not need special hazardous waste permits for storage prior to recycling.
affected_groups.group: Destination facilities storing lithium-ion batteries for recycling

affected_groups.effect: Must issue a new rule regarding the management of lithium-ion batteries as universal waste within 18 months.

key_provisions: Directs certain destination facilities that store lithium-ion batteries before recycling to follow specific requirements for large quantity handlers of universal waste rather than more stringent hazardous waste destination facility rules.
Requires the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to issue a new rule regarding the management of lithium-ion batteries as universal waste within 18 months of enactment.

Instructs the EPA Administrator to consider tailoring universal waste requirements for lithium-ion batteries, including safety requirements and regulatory changes to support critical mineral recovery while protecting health and the environment.
Updates the Mercury-Containing and Rechargeable Battery Management Act to reference part 273 of title 40 of the Code of Federal Regulations.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Battery Recycling for America's Competitive Economy Act (BRACE Act) changes how lithium-ion batteries are regulated under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act. It aims to make it easier to recycle lithium-ion batteries and recover critical minerals by allowing certain storage and recycling facilities to follow universal waste rules instead of stricter hazardous waste regulations.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters the regulatory burden for facilities handling end-of-life lithium-ion batteries by replacing hazardous waste storage rules with universal waste standards on an interim basis and mandating a permanent EPA rulemaking within 18 months, which affects how lithium-ion batteries are stored and recycled nationwide.
